name: Fix Worker Plan First Coding Slice
description: Replace writer-era roles with explicit api, maintenance-worker, and judge-worker runtime surfaces; add shared worker and queue truth; and move LLM execution onto judge-worker with durable replay and honest product status.

userStories.title: Define explicit runtime roles and capability helpers
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want explicit `api`, `maintenance-worker`, and `judge-worker` role capabilities so DuckDB ownership, maintenance work, judging, and owner proxying stop depending on writer-era role strings.
acceptanceCriteria: Add final production roles for `api`, `maintenance-worker`, and `judge-worker`, keeping `dev-single` only as a local combined-testing role if still needed.
Add capability helpers for DuckDB ownership, maintenance loops, judging loops, and owner proxy behavior instead of coarse writer checks.
`api` and `judge-worker` cannot claim owner-only work, while `maintenance-worker` candidates can own DuckDB.

userStories.title: Rename runtime and operator surfaces away from writer terminology
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want env names, runtime profiles, process identities, scripts, routes, and operator copy to use owner or maintenance-worker terminology so the shipped runtime no longer exposes writer-era contracts.
acceptanceCriteria: Rename writer-era env vars, runtime-profile names, process identities, service labels, heartbeat payloads, log labels, and operator routes to owner or maintenance-worker naming.

Package scripts, dev-watch helpers, local run docs, backend-availability probes, navigation warnings, and admin route names no longer refer to `writer`, `worker`, `SERVER_WRITER_URL`, or `/api/writer_connections`.
No shipped runtime behavior still branches on removed `writer` or `worker` role strings.
`bun test src/server/indexStartup.test.ts src/server/utils/runtimeLogger.test.ts scripts/runWithRuntimeProfile.test.ts src/utils/runtimeProfile.test.ts` passes.

userStories.title: Migrate persisted config and settings UI to maintenance-worker naming
userStories.description: As an operator, I want persisted config rows, local settings, stored types, and settings UI fields to use final maintenance-worker names so upgrades finish the naming cutover instead of carrying legacy aliases forward.
acceptanceCriteria: Add the one-time DuckDB and local `forska.settings.json` rewrite from writer-era config keys to maintenance-worker naming without keeping steady-state public aliases.
Settings UI, rebuild-tuning fields, stored schema types, and client queries use final maintenance-worker naming only.
First boot against pre-cutover config rewrites or replaces legacy settings without requiring manual cleanup.

userStories.title: Add the judge-worker durable journal identity contract
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want `judge-worker` startup to require a stable durable journal identity so accepted claims and completion outbox rows survive restarts and fail closed when the storage target is unsafe.
acceptanceCriteria: Make `JUDGE_WORKER_ID` and optional `JUDGE_WORKER_JOURNAL_PATH` the canonical runtime contract, with deterministic durable app-data path derivation from the id when the path is omitted.
`judge-worker` startup refuses to run when the resolved journal target is missing, unstable, unwritable, non-durable, or collides with another live worker.
Runtime profiles, stack scripts, and desktop startup pass the same journal-identity contract through unchanged.

userStories.title: Add cutover version refusal and legacy writer lease fencing
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want cutover-version checks and legacy writer lease fencing so the new split runtime refuses mixed-mode peers and unsafe lease takeover during the release.
acceptanceCriteria: Add cutover runtime version checks to owner-routed APIs, heartbeat flows, and lease metadata.
Startup refuses incompatible pre-cutover peers instead of attempting mixed-mode operation.
Lease adoption or replacement refuses when a legacy writer is still reachable or its lease is still fresh.

userStories.title: Split background startup and cron ownership by capability
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want maintenance loops, judging loops, and cron mounts to start by capability so the final role split keeps required background work on the right process after writer-role removal.
acceptanceCriteria: `startBackgroundWork()` starts maintenance and judging loops by capability instead of one coarse writer gate.
`fullTextJobsCron`, `fullTextConversionJobsCron`, and `nvidiaSmiCron` run only on `maintenance-worker` in the cutover slice.
`maintenance-worker` can start as DuckDB owner and `judge-worker` can start without DuckDB write ownership.

userStories.title: Restrict public API mounting and add readiness plus fail-closed route classification
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want only `api` to mount the public product API and I want readiness plus route classification to fail closed so split-role startup stays safe before every route is audited.
acceptanceCriteria: Only `api` mounts the public `/api/*` product route tree after cutover, while `maintenance-worker` and `judge-worker` stay on private RPC or diagnostics surfaces.
Add bootstrap-safe `GET /api/runtime/ready` and separate readiness from the renamed worker-registry surface.
Unclassified or owner-dependent routes fail closed to owner proxy instead of accidentally running locally on `api`.

userStories.title: Add read-only query helpers and mandatory ownerless backend validation
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want audited read-only helpers and mandatory ownerless backend validation so ownerless health routes stay honest without silently falling back to owner-capable database paths.
acceptanceCriteria: Audited `api-read-only` and `judge-worker` local-read flows use dedicated read-only helpers instead of owner-capable query or database service constructors.
Startup validates that each ownerless route has a configured ownerless-readable backend, with fail-closed fallback when live read-only DuckDB is unavailable or untrusted.
Runtime guards or boundary tests prevent silent fallback to owner-capable database helpers in read-only contexts.

userStories.title: Persist worker registry heartbeats and takeover intent
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want shared worker heartbeat and takeover records so any `api` process can see eligible maintenance capacity and whether owner loss means no candidate or takeover in progress.
acceptanceCriteria: `api`, `maintenance-worker`, and `judge-worker` heartbeat through owner-backed registry storage with role, capabilities, memory limit, throughput profile, and freshness.
Registry queries expose eligible maintenance consumers across local and non-local worker processes instead of only the handling process.
Standby maintenance candidates publish ownerless-readable takeover intent and owner-freshness state so owner loss can surface `takeover_in_progress` honestly.

userStories.title: Persist project-scoped queue progress and maintenance recovery state
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want shared project-scoped and queue-scoped progress records so review and import status derives from fresh claims, scopes, and recovery state instead of local counters or queue depth.
acceptanceCriteria: Persist fresh claim or lease rows for import and review work with project or article scope, required consumer role, `lastStartedAt`, `lastProgressedAt`, and freshness.
`processing` derives from fresh persisted claims or leases instead of queue depth or orphaned counters.
Shared projections include `retryAfterAt`, `recoveryMode`, and maintenance recovery context when those fields affect honest status.

userStories.title: Persist shared SQLite health and completion-handoff projections
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want shared judgment-job SQLite health and completion-handoff state so `api` can answer health honestly without local SQLite ownership and can show when judge completions are waiting on maintenance acknowledgment.
acceptanceCriteria: Persist shared judgment-job SQLite health fields for outbox and queue presence, WAL signals, projection freshness, and projection source.
Shared state includes pending completion-ack visibility and oldest unacked completion age for `judge-worker` handoff.
`api` answers from shared or read-only truth when it is fresh enough and otherwise returns explicit maintenance-unavailable responses instead of guessing from missing local SQLite state.

userStories.title: Expose capabilities, registry state, and backend mode in diagnostics
userStories.description: As an operator, I want worker diagnostics to show local intent, shared worker availability, and ownerless backend mode so I can understand why routes are blocked or where they are being served.
acceptanceCriteria: `/api/admin/worker-runtime-diagnostics` returns local role, server role, capabilities, DuckDB ownership, route-serving mode, ownerless backend choice, registry-derived eligible consumers, takeover state, and cutover refusal status.
Diagnostics also expose read-path mode and pending completion-ack visibility when that shared state is available.
Tests cover the new diagnostics payload shape.
Verify in browser that worker diagnostics show local capabilities and active worker registry clearly.

userStories.title: Make the review warnings API project-scoped and honest
userStories.description: As a user, I want review-warning status to reflect the requested project's real consumer and queue state so the UI stops showing unrelated work as active progress.
acceptanceCriteria: `/api/projectsreviewswarnings` exposes `requiredConsumerRole`, eligible and active consumer counts, `activeWorkCount`, `progressState`, `blockedReason`, `lastStartedAt`, `lastProgressedAt`, `retryAfterAt`, and `recoveryMode`.
The route derives those fields from project-scoped persisted claims or leases instead of pending count alone or unrelated project activity.
The route answers locally on `api` only when shared or read-only truth or the ownerless backend is sufficient to answer honestly.

userStories.title: Update review UIs to render blocked, queued, and processing states honestly
userStories.description: As a user, I want review pages to distinguish waiting, cooldown, and active processing states so the product stops presenting stalled indexing as generic progress.
acceptanceCriteria: Review UI consumers show `in progress` only when `progressState = 'processing'`.
Review empty states and warnings distinguish blocked, queued, stalled, failed or cooldown, and actively processing states.
UI copy explicitly covers waiting for a maintenance worker and cooling down after memory pressure.
Verify in browser that the review warning shows `waiting for maintenance worker` when no maintenance-worker heartbeat exists.

userStories.title: Make judgment job health and summary routes honest about maintenance ownership
userStories.description: As an operator, I want judgment-job health to distinguish blocked import, active import, cooldown, repair, and completion-ack backlog states so job status stays useful even when `api` does not own SQLite or DuckDB writes.
acceptanceCriteria: `/api/judgmentsjobs/:id/health` and `/api/judgmentsjobs-health` expose import consumer presence and counts, `progressState`, `blockedReason`, `lastStartedAt`, `lastProgressedAt`, `retryAfterAt`, and `recoveryMode`.
Health responses distinguish active import, blocked import, cooldown or breaker block, completion waiting for owner acknowledgment, and repair-required states.
Shared import and running-work summaries preserve the job's model and content-setting identity instead of collapsing incompatible work into one generic backlog.
Verify in browser that judgment job health distinguishes blocked import from active import.

userStories.title: Add immutable execution snapshots and owner-backed judgment APIs
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want immutable execution snapshots and owner-backed claim and completion endpoints so `judge-worker` can execute frozen work items without direct DuckDB writes or mutable input drift.
acceptanceCriteria: Persist write-once execution snapshots before claim issuance and carry `claimId`, `executionSnapshotId`, and `executionSnapshotHash` through claim and completion flows.
Add owner-backed claim, completion, control, and immutable snapshot-fetch endpoints that preserve full work-item identity and validate snapshot identity on completion.
Completion handlers reject snapshot mismatch instead of binding work to current mutable prompt, provider, or article state.

userStories.title: Move LLM execution onto judge-worker with durable replay-safe completion handoff
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want `judge-worker` to execute owner-issued claims and durably replay completions so maintenance stays the control plane while LLM work survives restarts and network failures.
acceptanceCriteria: `judge-worker` writes accepted claims and completion payloads to a durable local SQLite journal or outbox before callback and replays unacked completions on restart.
`judge-worker` executes owner-issued claims without direct DuckDB writes or local judgment-job SQLite ownership while `maintenance-worker` remains the queue source of truth.
Token-use summaries travel in the durable completion outbox and are applied exactly once through the owner-backed completion path.

userStories.title: Add split-role dev mode and end-to-end verification docs
userStories.description: As an operator, I want a documented split-role local stack so I can reproduce missing-maintenance, failover, readiness, journal-collision, and snapshot-fallback behavior before shipping the cutover.
acceptanceCriteria: Runtime scripts can start `api`, `maintenance-worker`, and `judge-worker` together without manual file edits.

Local docs cover readiness versus worker-registry, missing-maintenance behavior, same-host maintenance failover, cutover refusal, judge-worker journal collision, and immutable snapshot-fetch fallback.
Runtime verification proves readiness stays bootstrap-safe, public and private route surfaces remain correct, and replay or fail-closed startup behaviors work as documented.
Verify at runtime that `GET /api/runtime/ready` stays usable while the worker-registry route reports missing maintenance or takeover in progress.
Verify at runtime that startup rejects incompatible writer-era peers or fresh reachable legacy writer leases.
Verify at runtime that a second `judge-worker` started with the same journal path refuses startup and that restarting with the same durable identity replays unacked completions.
Verify at runtime that disabling live read-only DuckDB still leaves ownerless routes answerable through the configured ownerless backend.
